issue_context.title: Define in-tree PluginConfig Args as component config types
issue_context.body:
/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

As we move from parameters in the root of the component config to using args in PluginConfig (#87617), we are losing visibility of available parameters (in the API definition) and their early validation. Arguably, we might also lose versioning.

Since the configuration of in-tree plugins is part of the API, one alternative is to move the args definition to the `pkg/scheduler/apis/config` package and their versioned counterparts.

Extracted from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87725#issuecomment-581519825

/cc @ahg-g @Huang-Wei
comments: +1 to having all plugin configuration definitions of in-tree plugins to the apis/config package. They are practically part of the API, and so we should make sure they are properly versioned.
+1 to hold plugin specific parameters in their own pluginConfig. Some parameter (e.g., `HardPodAffinitySymmetricWeight`) doesn't really make sense to be held at the root level.
Since there is no consensus, I'll add this as a discussion item for next SIG meeting.

Actually, let me add some clarification:
This question is not referring to keeping `hardPodAffinitySymmetricWeight` in the root of `KubeSchedulerConfig`. We already decided to just use PluginConfig for that (#87657)
The proposal here is to move the definition of the struct `interpodaffinity.Args` to `pkg/scheduler/apis/config` (probably as something like `InterPodAffinityArgs`) and to its versioned counterparts. The appeal is that of versioning and perhaps early validation.

PluginConfigs of the various in-tree plugins are part of the scheduler's config api, so ```pkg/scheduler/apis/config``` seems the natural place for it.

we could place them in a subdirectory or file under ```pkg/scheduler/apis/config```.

> The proposal here is to move the definition of the struct interpodaffinity.Args to pkg/scheduler/apis/config (probably as something like InterPodAffinityArgs) and to its versioned counterparts.

I suppose the `runtime.Unknown` type of `PluginConfig.Args` remains unchanged, right? i.e., it still accepts arbitrary bytes data, and decoded into particular Args type in runtime. It's just the particular Args are going to be held in a versioned manner.
Yes, we are not changing the current API. We are just declaring that whatever we parse from ```runtime.Unknown``` for a specific plugin is versioned and is part of the api.

Update from SIG meeting: we are onboard with this change.

I'll work on it (or open for contributors) once multi scheduler profiles land.
/assign

I'm trying to wrap my head around conversion and defaults once we move these types.

In particular, I'm thinking of building an scheme in `pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1` that has all the in-tree plugin args registered. My hope is that with this scheme we can make [`DecodeInto`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fe9073b8c14bbf6bbe42a2259f01d3d3a853a6a3/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1/registry.go#L31) use the scheme for in-tree plugins and resort to Unmarshal for out-of-tree plugins.

However, arg types don't have `metav1.TypeMeta`. They shouldn't need it, as they are supposed to only be specified in a `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io` file, and evolve with it.
So, I wonder if we can make it work, given that we would be providing a typed struct to `DecodeInto`. My fear is that the scheme wouldn't be able to do the conversion from v1alpha2, where we would define the json annotations and defaults.

@liggitt, could you shed some light?

I don't like option 1, seems strange to pass around version and kind around in the scheduler, but it might be the easiest option to move forward with. 

When I proposed moving plugin Args to ```apis/config``` my initial thought was that we will do something like option 2. But I like option 2.i since we will do the conversion once, and we will do it in the proper place, however we need to understand better how we plan to handle out-of-tree plugins.

>  We still use runtime.Unknown if it is out-of-tree plugin.

How will the conversion function know that a given plugin args is one for an out-of-tree plugin? if decoding fails, or we can use the in-tree registry I guess, and where do you propose we store those? in a separate plugin args slice? That will make the framework instantiation logic not pretty.

> How will the conversion function know that a given plugin args is one for an out-of-tree plugin?

We would already have the structs in`types.go`, so I don't see any harm on having a private map (or even a `switch` statement) that is keyed by the plugin name to the type. Or we can have this slice in `pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/registry.go`, except that we build the registry at init time.
Any further questions? I would like to get this fixed early in the development cycle of 1.19.
Is the expectation that all plugins and their args will be compiled-in?
Yes. But only in-tree plugins would have their types versioned in `k8s.io/kube-scheduler`
/assign

We came up with the following solution in an offline discussion with @liggitt:

1. Move the Arg types to the versioned and internal component config types #88585
1. Migrate from `runtime.Unknown` to `runtime.RawExtension` for the `PluginConfig.Args` external (v1alpha2) type and to `runtime.Object` for the internal type. This is backwards compatible. This combination of types will allow us to have parsed types for in-tree plugins and still deliver raw bytes to out-of-tree plugins #89904
1. Implement `DecodeNestedObjects(d runtime.Decoder) error` for `v1alpha2.KubeSchedulerConfiguration` to decode the raw bytes into the known arg types.
1. Move defaulting of plugin args into the versioned packages.
Thanks Aldo for the wrap-up!

/reopen

We still have pending work here :)

@alculquicondor: Reopened this issue.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87784#issuecomment-611638750):

For this and all `${PLUGIN}Args`.

- add TypeMeta field (see KubeSchedulerConfig type)
- add a deepcopy-gen comment (see KubeSchedulerConfig type)
- register the type in `staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/config/v1alpha2/register.go`
Done
why is this mixing internal config types (NewPluginConfig) with external config types (schedulerv1alpha2.NodeResourcesFitArgs)?

This is temporary. The next step is to make the plugins only handle the internal types. For that, we need to do the conversion of user provided args into the internal types during the initial parsing of component config, as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87784#issuecomment-592709524

The idea behind this PR here was to make the plugin arg types versioned. One can argue that the args of the internal scheduler plugins are a part of the API and therefore should be versioned. The conversion was supposed to be addressed in the v1.19 release cycle.  

The internal types map 1:1 to the API, external ones. However, only the external are annotated with JSON tags.
talked through the plan for shifting plugins to internal types with @alculquicondor, this is ok as an interim step
This should temporary. Add a comment just in case.
I'm not sure if a comment would reduce confusion. If it does, it should be also added to other places in this - and potentially other - files. What would you say here?
You are right. Instead add a note in the PR description saying that we are using external types temporarily and that there will be a follow up PR.

For this and all `${PLUGIN}Args`.

- add TypeMeta field (see KubeSchedulerConfig type)
- add a deepcopy-gen comment (see KubeSchedulerConfig type)
- register the type in `pkg/scheduler/apis/config//register.go`
Done
this was previously decoding into an internal type with no json tags?
are there any tests exercising loading this config?
oh... the "internal" type defined json tags on `config.RequestedToCapacityRatioArguments`, but not on `config.ResourceSpec` and `config.UtilizationShapePoint`

check what happens with the following args in 1.18 for this plugin:

```yaml
shape: [{"Utilization": 1, "Score": 1}, {"utilization": 2, "score": 2}]
resources: [{"Name":"a","Weight":1},{"Name":"b","Weight":2}]
```

True. There is nothing exercising these E2E. It is non-trivial given how buried the types are.

I think the json decoder would simply ignore casing. @pancernik, could you verify this?

We can add the test in `requested_to_capacity_ratio_test.go`, as there is no other location that would go through the decoding. I'll add the test in the compatibility tests once we move the decoding to the component config files.

Surprisingly, Go's [JSON encoding](https://golang.org/pkg/encoding/json/#Unmarshal):
> matches incoming object keys to the keys used by Marshal (either the struct field name or its 
tag), preferring an exact match but also accepting a case-insensitive match

I did confirm this when working on this PR.  Wouldn't adding this test add some confusion to the future readers? This test would actually test a documented behaviour of the language stdlib. What do you think @alculquicondor @liggitt ?

yes, please add the test and I'll move it to compatibility tests when we are ready.

But leave the types that didn't have json tags without them in v1alpha2 with a comment to fix them in v1beta1.
The stdlib behavior is problematic, and API type decoding is explicitly case-sensitive. We need the test to make sure we don't break compatibility with v1alpha2 configurations.
The test was added and the types were copied to v1alpha2 without json tags from the second level.

Use internal version from `"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/apis/config"`

The internal versions do not have json tags. And the versioned API types can be used when creating the configuration files for the in-tree plugins.

If we use the internal types here, we'd need to test them as the plugin code would use them. And we would also have to keep a separate set of tests for the API types as somebody might use them to generate plugin configuration.

Please note that this will change once the decisions around conversions are made in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/88093. And the long term goal is to use the internal types here.

SG.
nit: I'd prefer to keep these fields in `pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go`.
I had the same preference. @alculquicondor why did you think it's better to have a separate file?
Just to keep a file from growing too much.
Ditto. Use internal version from `"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/apis/config"`.

You should use the unversioned API here:

```suggestion
	NodeLabelArgs *config.NodeLabelArgs
```

This applies to all similar occurrences in this file.
